passages.text: Meanwhile, Joseph had been taken down to Egypt, where an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was taken down to Egypt.
Potiphar was an Egyptian man.
Potiphar served as an officer of Pharaoh.
Potiphar was the captain of the guard.
The Ishmaelites brought Joseph to Egypt.
Potiphar bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites.
passages.original: וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הוּרַ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה וַיִּקְנֵ֡הוּ פּוֹטִיפַר֩ סְרִ֨יס פַּרְעֹ֜ה שַׂ֤ר הַטַּבָּחִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מִיַּד֙ הַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹרִדֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, serving in the household of his Egyptian master.
passages.sermon: The LORD was with Joseph.\r\nJoseph became a successful man.\r\nJoseph served in the house of his Egyptian master.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְהִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ וַיְהִ֕י בְּבֵ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו הַמִּצְרִֽי׃

passages.text: When his master saw that the LORD was with him and made him prosper in all he did, Joseph found favor in his sight and became his personal attendant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household and entrusted him with everything he owned.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a servant in Egypt.
His master was Potiphar.
Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh.
Potiphar was captain of the guard.
Potiphar saw that the LORD was with Joseph.
Potiphar saw that the LORD made Joseph succeed in everything he did.
Joseph found favor in Potiphar’s eyes.
Joseph served Potiphar.
Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his house.
Potiphar gave Joseph control over everything he owned.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲדֹנָ֔יו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁר־ ה֣וּא עֹשֶׂ֔ה יְהוָ֖ה מַצְלִ֥יחַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃ וַיִּמְצָ֨א יוֹסֵ֥ף חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינָ֖יו וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹת֑וֹ וַיַּפְקִדֵ֙הוּ֙ עַל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וְכָל־ יֶשׁ־ ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: From the time that he put Joseph in charge of his household and all he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s household on account of him. The LORD’s blessing was on everything he owned, both in his house and in his field.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a servant in Egypt.
His master was an Egyptian.
His master put Joseph in charge of his house.
His master gave Joseph authority over everything he owned.
From that time, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house.
The LORD blessed the Egyptian because of Joseph.
The LORD’s blessing was on everything the Egyptian owned.
The LORD blessed what was in the house.
The LORD blessed what was in the field.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֡י מֵאָז֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֹת֜וֹ בְּבֵית֗וֹ וְעַל֙ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ ל֔וֹ וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֞י בִּרְכַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ בְּכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ ל֔וֹ בַּבַּ֖יִת וּבַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: So Potiphar left all that he owned in Joseph’s care; he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was well-built and handsome, and after some time his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.”
passages.sermon:
Potiphar was Joseph’s master.
Potiphar trusted Joseph completely.
Potiphar left everything he owned in Joseph’s care.
Potiphar did not concern himself with anything in his house.
Potiphar only thought about the food he ate.
Joseph was well-built.
Joseph was handsome.
After some time, Potiphar’s wife noticed Joseph.
Potiphar’s wife looked at Joseph with desire.
Potiphar’s wife said to Joseph, “Sleep with me.”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ לוֹ֮ בְּיַד־ יוֹסֵף֒ וְלֹא־ יָדַ֤ע אִתּוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־ הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁר־ ה֣וּא אוֹכֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף יְפֵה־ תֹ֖אַר וִיפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃ וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַתִּשָּׂ֧א אֵֽשֶׁת־ אֲדֹנָ֛יו אֶת־ עֵינֶ֖יהָ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֑ף וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שִׁכְבָ֥ה עִמִּֽי׃

passages.text: But he refused. “Look,” he said to his master’s wife, “with me here, my master does not concern himself with anything in his house, and he has entrusted everything he owns to my care.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew slave in Egypt.
Potiphar was Joseph’s master.
Potiphar’s wife asked Joseph to sleep with her.
Joseph refused her request.
Joseph spoke to Potiphar’s wife.
Joseph said, “My master does not concern himself with anything in this house when I am here.
My master has put everything he owns into my care.”
passages.original: וַיְמָאֵ֓ן׀ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ אֵ֣שֶׁת אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־ יָדַ֥ע אִתִּ֖י מַה־ בַּבָּ֑יִת וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ יֶשׁ־ ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדִֽי׃

passages.text: No one in this house is greater than I am. He has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. So how could I do such a great evil and sin against God?”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a servant in Potiphar’s house.
Potiphar trusted Joseph with everything he owned.
No one in this house is greater than I am.
My master has not kept anything from me except you.
You are his wife.
How could I do this great evil?
How could I sin against God?
passages.original: אֵינֶ֨נּוּ גָד֜וֹל בַּבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּה֮ מִמֶּנִּי֒ וְלֹֽא־ חָשַׂ֤ךְ מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־ אוֹתָ֖ךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתְּ־ אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨יךְ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֜ה הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְחָטָ֖אתִי לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: Although Potiphar’s wife spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her or even be near her.
passages.sermon:
Potiphar’s wife spoke to Joseph every day.
She asked him to lie with her.
Joseph refused her requests.
He would not go to bed with her.
He would not even be near her.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כְּדַבְּרָ֥הּ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֖ף י֣וֹם׀ י֑וֹם וְלֹא־ שָׁמַ֥ע אֵלֶ֛יהָ לִשְׁכַּ֥ב אֶצְלָ֖הּ לִהְי֥וֹת עִמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: One day, however, Joseph went into the house to attend to his work, and not a single household servant was inside.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew slave in Egypt.
Potiphar was his master.
Joseph was in charge of Potiphar’s house.
One day, Joseph entered the house.
He went in to do his work.
No one else from the household was inside.
No servant was present in the house.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ כְּהַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א הַבַּ֖יְתָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת מְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨ין אִ֜ישׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת שָׁ֖ם בַּבָּֽיִת׃

passages.text: She grabbed Joseph by his cloak and said, “Sleep with me!” But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.
passages.sermon:
Potiphar’s wife grabbed Joseph by his cloak.
She said, “Sleep with me!”
Joseph left his cloak in her hand.
He escaped from her.
He ran outside.
passages.original: וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂ֧הוּ בְּבִגְד֛וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר שִׁכְבָ֣ה עִמִּ֑י וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃

passages.text: When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house, she called her household servants. “Look,” she said, “this Hebrew has been brought to us to make sport of us. He came to me so he could sleep with me, but I screamed as loud as I could.
passages.sermon:
Potiphar’s wife saw Joseph’s cloak in her hand.
She saw that Joseph had run out of the house.
She called the servants of her household.
She spoke to them.
She said, “Look at this.
They brought a Hebrew man to us.
He came here to make fun of us.
He came to me and wanted to sleep with me.
I screamed with a loud voice.”
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ כִּרְאוֹתָ֔הּ כִּֽי־ עָזַ֥ב בִּגְד֖וֹ בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַיָּ֖נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃ וַתִּקְרָ֞א לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵיתָ֗הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר רְא֗וּ הֵ֥בִיא לָ֛נוּ אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י לְצַ֣חֶק בָּ֑נוּ בָּ֤א אֵלַי֙ לִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמִּ֔י וָאֶקְרָ֖א בְּק֥וֹל גָּדֽוֹל׃

passages.text: When he heard me scream for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
passages.sermon:
Potiphar’s wife spoke about Joseph.
Joseph was a Hebrew slave in Potiphar’s house.
She said, “I screamed for help.
He heard me scream.
He left his cloak beside me.
He ran out of the house.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י כְשָׁמְע֔וֹ כִּֽי־ הֲרִימֹ֥תִי קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ אֶצְלִ֔י וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃

passages.text: So Potiphar’s wife kept Joseph’s cloak beside her until his master came home.
passages.sermon: Potiphar’s wife took Joseph’s cloak.\r\nShe kept the cloak with her.\r\nShe kept it until Joseph’s master came home.
passages.original: וַתַּנַּ֥ח בִּגְד֖וֹ אֶצְלָ֑הּ עַד־ בּ֥וֹא אֲדֹנָ֖יו אֶל־ בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then she told him the same story: “The Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me, but when I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
passages.sermon:
Potiphar’s wife spoke to her husband.
She told him what happened.
She said, “The Hebrew slave came to me.
You brought this slave into our house.
He tried to make fun of me.
I screamed for help.
When I screamed, he left his cloak beside me.
He ran out of the house.”
passages.original: וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּֽא־ אֵלַ֞י הָעֶ֧בֶד הָֽעִבְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבֵ֥אתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְצַ֥חֶק בִּֽי׃ וַיְהִ֕י כַּהֲרִימִ֥י קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֥ב בִּגְד֛וֹ אֶצְלִ֖י וַיָּ֥נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃

passages.text: When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, “This is what your slave did to me,” he burned with anger.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew slave in Egypt.
Potiphar was Joseph’s master.
Potiphar’s wife accused Joseph of wrongdoing.
She told Potiphar a story about Joseph.
She said, “Your slave did these things to me.”
Potiphar listened to his wife’s words.
Potiphar became very angry.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹנָ֜יו אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּרָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עָ֥שָׂהּ לִ֖י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Joseph’s master took him and had him thrown into the prison where the king’s prisoners were confined. While Joseph was there in the prison, the LORD was with him and extended kindness to him, granting him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew slave in Egypt.
Joseph’s master was Potiphar.
Potiphar took Joseph.
Potiphar put Joseph into prison.
This prison was where the king’s prisoners stayed.
Joseph stayed in that prison.
The LORD was with Joseph.
The LORD showed kindness to Joseph.
The LORD made the prison warden like Joseph.
The prison warden saw Joseph with favor.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲדֹנֵ֨י יוֹסֵ֜ף אֹת֗וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֔הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ אֲסוּרֵי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲסוּרִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי־ שָׁ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃ וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיֵּ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו חָ֑סֶד וַיִּתֵּ֣ן חִנּ֔וֹ בְּעֵינֵ֖י שַׂ֥ר בֵּית־ הַסֹּֽהַר׃

passages.text: And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care, so that he was responsible for all that was done in the prison.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a prisoner in Egypt.
The warden was the chief officer of the prison.
The warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care.
Joseph became responsible for every prisoner in the prison.
The warden gave Joseph authority over everything done in the prison.
Joseph did all the work that needed to be done there.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֞ן שַׂ֤ר בֵּית־ הַסֹּ֙הַר֙ בְּיַד־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת כָּל־ הָ֣אֲסִירִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹשִׂים֙ שָׁ֔ם ה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: The warden did not concern himself with anything under Joseph’s care, because the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew slave in Egypt.
Joseph’s master put him in prison.
The prison warden was responsible for the prisoners.
The warden gave Joseph authority over everything in the prison.
The warden did not watch or worry about anything Joseph managed.
The LORD was with Joseph.
The LORD helped Joseph.
The LORD made everything Joseph did succeed.
passages.original: אֵ֣ין׀ שַׂ֣ר בֵּית־ הַסֹּ֗הַר רֹאֶ֤ה אֶֽת־ כָּל־ מְא֙וּמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וַֽאֲשֶׁר־ ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה מַצְלִֽיחַ׃ס
